cohort: The study involved singleton pregnancies delivered between 24 and 28 weeks of gestation, divided into groups based on intended mode of delivery.
finding: The study found no significant difference in neonatal death or other composite adverse neonatal outcomes between trial of labor and upfront cesarean delivery for singletons born at 24-28 weeks gestation.
mod_finding: No significant difference in neonatal death or composite adverse outcomes was observed between trial of labor and upfront cesarean delivery for singleton infants born at 24-28 weeks gestation.
